title: Field ops value-prop matrix - LLM endpoints
body:
TL;DR: Field-facing quick matrix that maps customer persona -> core value props -> competitor talking points -> two short rebut scripts and a demo hook. Use this to tailor 5–10 min pre-call notes and to feed SDR/AE playbooks. Not a competitor encyclopedia; focus on high-conviction contrasts where Redwood’s production-first platform converts mid-market/enterprise deals.

Audience and use cases:
- Primary: AE + Solutions Engineers preparing for discovery and technical validation calls with product/platform leads.
- Secondary: SDRs for qualifying call scripts, CS for handoff notes.

How to use this doc:
1) Pick persona row (Infra lead / ML Eng / Product PM).
2) Read top 3 value props and the one-sentence competitor Achilles’ heel.
3) Adapt the 30s rebut and 90s demo hook before the call.

Persona matrix (short form)
- Infra Lead (SRE/Platform)
  - Pain: Unpredictable latency spikes, noisy multi-tenant capacity, lack of SLA for inference.
  - Redwood value props: Dedicated capacity with SLA, smart routing/fallbacks, kernel/runtime optimizations that reduce tail latency.
  - Competitor tilt: Large cloud endpoints sell general-purpose autoscaling but hide tail variability and queueing behavior.
  - 30s rebut: "Totally — autoscaling helps average throughput, but customers tell us the hard bit is tail latency when cold-starts and KV cache churn happen. Redwood gives dedicated pools and routes by policy so you get predictable p99s during peak traffic."
  - 90s demo hook: Show Console dashboard: p50/p90/p99 traces for two routes, toggle from shared to dedicated and show latency stabilization.

- ML Engineer (Model owner)
  - Pain: Need to iterate model variants quickly, want consistent behavior across dev->prod, worried about token costs for heavy experiments.
  - Redwood value props: Model versioning + rollout policies, cost-aware quantization suggestions, KV/prefix caching and eval hooks.
  - Competitor tilt: Some API providers make it easy to get started but offer limited rollout controls or opaque cost signals.
  - 30s rebut: "We surface per-route token economics and recommend quant/profile changes by workload so you can experiment without surprising bills."
  - 90s demo hook: Show Optimize recommendations for a sample 8k-seq workload and compare estimated token costs across model variants.

- Product Manager
  - Pain: Need reliable behavior for chat assistants, audit logs for compliance, and gradual rollouts to avoid regressions.
  - Redwood value props: Rollouts with canary and automatic fallback, structured output + function-calling primitives, audit logs and private deployments.
  - Competitor tilt: Some LLM APIs move fast on features but lack enterprise rollout/trace tooling.
  - 30s rebut: "If a single regression breaks a user flow, the business cost is immediate. Our rollout + eval hooks let you catch regressions on a small percentage before full rollouts."
  - 90s demo hook: Walk through creating a canary, attaching an eval suite, and showing automatic rollback on quality regression.

Competitor quick sketches (for call prep)
- OpenAI-style large API providers
  - Strengths: Broad model catalog, strong developer mindshare, simple dev experience.
  - Weaknesses: Limited guarantees on latency/cost for high-volume production, limited private deployment options for regulated customers.
  - Field angle: "We match the dev experience but add predictable economics and dedicated SLAs for production traffic."

- Anthropic-like safety-first models
  - Strengths: Safety-centric models and guardrails, good for compliance-conscious use cases.
  - Weaknesses: May trade off throughput/latency or have limited routing/burst capacity options.
  - Field angle: "If safety is primary, you get great models; if you need throughput and predictable latency at scale, Redwood layers routing and dedicated capacity while integrating safety controls."

- Cloud vendor managed endpoints (AWS/GCP/Azure)
  - Strengths: Integrations with broader infra, familiar procurement.
  - Weaknesses: Primitive inference-specific UX, cost opacity, and model lifecycle tooling gaps.
  - Field angle: "You can run inference on cloud infra, but the specialized runtime + compile/kernal selection we provide materially improves p99 latency and cost per token for real traffic shapes."

Traps and landmines (what to avoid saying)
- Don’t claim "best model quality" — we position performance and production economics, not raw SOTA model comparisons.
- Avoid deep product architecture debates in early calls; keep language at policy/UX level and save infra deep-dives for SEs.
- Don’t commit to features not GA: if asked about on-prem roadmap specifics, use can’t-share timelines and offer to co-sell with Solutions Engineering.

Top objections + short scripts
- "We’re happy with our current cloud endpoint."
  - Script: "Great — how predictable is your p99 under peak? If you’ve seen variability, we can show a 30-minute side-by-side of identical traffic that demonstrates stabilization with dedicated pools and routing policies."
- "Migration cost is too high."
  - Script: "We provide import hooks and a compatibility layer; many teams run a hybrid where critical routes go to Redwood Dedicated while legacy traffic stays on the incumbent during phased cutover."
- "We use managed vendor because of procurement."
  - Script: "We work with procurement and have marketplace/contract options; for regulated workloads we also offer private deployments that map to existing security controls."

Demo/POC play suggestions (30–90 minute engagements)
- Quick benchmark POC (30m prep + 60m run): Baseline their current endpoint with a representative trace, route identical traffic to Redwood Dedicated, show token cost delta and p99 improvement. Deliverable: short doc with graphs and 3 recommended knobs.
- Canary safety + rollback POC (90m): Hook their canary route, attach an eval suite, trigger a regression and show automated rollback. Deliverable: recorded artifact + config snippet for their CI.

Competitive differentiators to emphasize (elevator lines)
- Predictable production economics: "We make inference predictable via routing, caching, and per-route cost signals — so unit economics are a conscious control, not a surprise."
- Unified surface across environments: "Same API and rollout semantics whether hosted, dedicated, or private — reduces friction for regulated or multi-region customers."
- Observability that matters: "Per-token tracing, eval hooks and rollout analytics let you correlate quality/regressions to model changes quickly."

Open questions to surface to PM/SE before finalizing talk track:
- Which routes are latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive? (need sample traffic shapes)
- Any regulatory/compliance constraints that force private deployment?
- Current model catalog and quantization tolerance?

Appendix: Scripts for role-play (useful to practice)
- SDR 20s: "Hi — quick q: when you hit peak inference traffic, do you see unpredictable tail latency or surprising bills? We help teams stabilize p99s and make unit cost visible — is that something your platform team owns?"
- AE opening 45s: "We help engineering-led teams ship LLM features without building a custom inference layer. For product teams that scale from prototype to millions of requests, our focus is predictable latency, per-route economics, and controls for canary/rollback. Curious what your current pain is around reliability vs cost?"

Notes and proof points to call out (bring the data)
- p99 improvement ranges we typically show in POC: 20–60% for cacheable chat workloads when moving to dedicated + KV caching.
- Typical token-cost delta from quant/recommendations: 10–30% for CPU-friendly quant profiles on static scoring workloads.
- Reference logos for industry proof (use customer-approved list) and a one-pager for compliance packages.
